note: An ancestor chart for Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen, who is where this archive starts and works backwards from. Every box is a person a document names. A WALL is a place where the archive knows a person existed and cannot name their parents — and the reasons differ. Where a man married twice, only the mother of the next box can stand in the chart; the other marriage is noted against him, because in this family it is usually the second marriage that explains the children.

alt.why: His second marriage, unnamed on his own 1884 death notice and named at last by a christening — the 1870 Doop Register enters the parents as “Petrus Jacobus Booyzen en Johanna Margaritha Pretorius”. Two more sons, neither of them in this chart.

A second marriage, and a second van der Merwe — named as the mother on their son Hendrik Stephanus's 1908 death notice, whose age puts his birth about June 1828. She is not the mother of the box below her. She is the reason the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis cannot all share one.

f.wall: No father. No dates. Nothing behind the button.
No estate file for her in the Cape archives. Searched eight ways.

Documented as his WIFE and as a mother — her son David Schalk was baptised on 4 January 1807 — but NOT documented as the mother of the box below her. The 1876 Sterfkennis names eight children and no mother for any of them, and a second van der Merwe wife bore a ninth about 1828.
“Names of the Parents of the Deceased. Not Known.” Written 1840, thirteen years after he died.

alt.why: Her first husband, dead before 1817. The relative who completed James Montjoy's death notice could name him — and still could not name Montjoy's own parents.

f.wall: One profile holding two men — a Yorkshire farmer of Bilsdale and a man who died at de Bruins Poort. His son's 1903 registration says only: an Irishman, born in Ireland.

f.same: His parents are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe — two boxes already standing on the father's side of this chart. The line folds back on itself here, and that fold is the cousin marriage.
